subject: Finovia - SLA compensation matrix & latency tolerance
messages:
From: Peter Stone <peter.stone@finovia.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finovia.com
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA expectations for pilot

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Finovia is excited to move a small production pilot onto Redwood next month. Before we lock dates, procurement asked me to confirm a few SLA items so our SOC and finance teams can greenlight the purchase order. High level we need: an uptime commitment, monthly service credit table, and a latency SLO for API endpoints used by our customer-facing product.

Two asks from our side:
- Can the standard uptime be set at 99.9% for the pilot (we understand enterprise customers have tighter numbers)?
- We need a clear monthly credit matrix (example: % credit for certain availability bands) with a hard cap so our accounting can model worst-case.

Also, is there a carveout for scheduled maintenance (we typically require a 72 hour lookahead for planned windows)? And for latency: we expect p95 under 400ms for read endpoints — if that needs to be an exception for bursty batch jobs we can note those separately.

Attached is our internal procurement template for reference. Can you provide a proposed SLA template or redline?

Best,
Peter
Peter Stone
Head of Platform Operations, Finovia
Peter.Stone@finovia.com

Attachment: finovia_procurement_template.pdf (referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Stone <peter.stone@finovia.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA expectations for pilot

Peter — thanks, and congrats to the Finovia team on moving this forward. Attaching a short, customer-friendly SLA excerpt and a suggested monthly compensation matrix for a pilot (see redline_sla_finovia.pdf). Summary here so procurement can triage quickly:

Proposal (pilot-specific):
- Uptime target: 99.90% monthly (pilot period only). Standard enterprise template retains 99.95% for paid production tiers.
- Monthly credit bands (percentage of monthly invoice):
  - 99.95% - 100.00%: 0% credit
  - 99.90% - 99.95%: 5% credit
  - 99.00% - 99.90%: 15% credit
  - < 99.00%: 30% credit (maximum cap)
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 400ms for the customer-facing read endpoints. For batch or long-running endpoints we propose a separate latency carveout documented in the runbook.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (we provide >= 48 hours notice for maintenance windows impacting the pilot), force majeure, and customer-caused issues.
- Additional guardrails: credits are capped at 100% of the monthly invoice (i.e., cannot exceed what you paid us that month).

Next steps I suggest: 1) review the attached redline, 2) let us know any absolute dealbreakers (credit cap or exclusions), 3) if acceptable we’ll generate a DocuSign for signature and schedule a joint runbook session.

Cc'ing Laura (VP, Sales) and Marissa (Customer Success) for alignment on credit cap and operational runbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Attachment: redline_sla_finovia.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SLA expectations for pilot

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the draft. A couple internal asks before we send final to Finovia:

1) Cap: I think a 30% max credit for the <99.0% bucket is too open for a pilot. Can we lower the absolute monthly cap to 25% of the invoice for the pilot, with an option to revisit at the production negotiation?

2) Maintenance carveout: Procurement asked about our notice window. We usually do >= 48 hours but can accept a 72 hour notice for any maintenance that could impact Finovia's customer-facing SLA during the pilot. Let's put that in the redline.

3) Onset clause: For the pilot only, recommend SLA credits apply only after the first 30 days of go-live to allow for tuning and KV/cache warm-up. That protects Redwood from immature traffic patterns driving credits.

If those three items are acceptable, I’m comfortable we send a near-final. Marissa — legal sign-off? If legal is ok with 25% pilot cap and the 30-day onset, please say so and Karthik can send final to Peter.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA expectations for pilot

Laura — legal is comfortable with the compromise but asks that the 25% cap be explicitly phrased as "maximum monthly compensation" and that the onset clause is limited to the first paid month (i.e., applies only to the first 30 days after go-live). Also adding a clause that credits are deducted from future invoices rather than refunded.

One more ops request: add a short line in the runbook stating that latency carveouts for batch jobs are per-endpoint and require an agreed SLAB (service-level adjustment) noted in the onboarding checklist. That prevents generalizing the exception across the API surface.

If Karthik can fold these into the redline, we can present to Finovia as the final-for-signature.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Stone <peter.stone@finovia.com>, procurement@finovia.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Final SLA for pilot: Finovia (signature request)

Peter — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review we've updated the pilot SLA to reflect Finovia's ask plus a few protective guardrails for Redwood. Summary of the signed-off changes (see attached SLA_Final_for_Signature.pdf):

- Uptime target for pilot: 99.90% monthly.
- Monthly compensation matrix:
  - 99.95% - 100.00%: 0% credit
  - 99.90% - 99.95%: 5% credit
  - 99.00% - 99.90%: 15% credit
  - < 99.00%: 25% credit (maximum monthly compensation for the pilot)
- Credits are applied as invoice adjustments to future invoices (not as cash refunds). Credits are capped at the customer’s monthly invoice for the affected month.
- Latency: p95 <= 400ms for customer-facing read endpoints. Batch/long-running endpoints will be documented with per-endpoint SLABs in the onboarding runbook.
- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood will provide >= 72 hours notice for any maintenance that could impact the pilot SLA.
- Onset clause: SLA remedies apply starting 30 days after go-live for the pilot.

Action item: if the summary looks good please sign the attached document via DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/abc123-finovia-sla. Once signed we’ll schedule the pre-launch runbook call and confirm go-live dates.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the redlines.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: SLA_Final_for_Signature.pdf
